transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Well, I... I came in because I know the people at my apartment are watching my comings and goings. They're slipping notes about me to the office. Everybody keeps telling me it's just regular notices on the doors, like maintenance things, but I know better. It's like that time back in '98 when I lived in that duplex on 4th Street, you know? The landlord there, he had this weird dog, a beagle mix I think, that just stared at me all day. I used to work at the hardware store down the road back then, before my back got bad. Anyway, the notes here are definitely about me.
Besides noticing these notes, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people don't seem to hear, or seen things that others don't see?

No, I don't hear anything like that. No voices or anything. It's just the notes, mostly. But you know, speaking of hearing things, my neighbor's TV is always on so loud. He watches those old westerns, the ones with John Wayne. I used to watch those with my dad when I was a kid. We had this big box TV, took up half the living room. Dad always said they don't make movies like that anymore. He was a mechanic, worked on Fords mostly. Had grease under his fingernails that never washed out. But no, I don't hear voices. Just that TV sometimes.
How long have you felt that your neighbors are watching you and leaving notes about you—has this been going on for weeks, or longer, like months or years?

Well, let's see... it's been going on for a while now. I'd say about a year and a month that I've known they were watching me and leaving those notes. Started right around the time the weather started turning cold last year. I remember because I had to get my heavy coat out of storage. It's a good coat, got it at a second-hand shop downtown. The zipper sticks a little at the bottom, but it's warm. The lady who sold it to me, she had the brightest red hair I've ever seen. Reminded me of my Aunt Sally. She used to make the best peach cobbler every summer. But yeah, about a year and a month since the notes started.
Has this concern about being watched affected your ability to keep up with daily activities—like your job, taking care of yourself, or spending time with friends and family?

Well, yeah, it really has. I mean, I've fallen way behind on my bills, and I keep missing my doctor appointments. I just... I can't keep my days straight anymore, you know? And I stopped going to church, stopped doing my volunteer work. I just can't trust people when I talk to them, always wondering what they're really up to. Speaking of church, though, we used to have this pastor, Pastor Miller. He drove this old Buick, baby blue. It had a rusted bumper that rattled every time he pulled into the parking lot. He always smelled like peppermint and old books. Used to give out those little hard candies to the kids after service. I remember one time, it rained so hard the church basement flooded, and we all had to use buckets to bail the water out. Took us three days to get it dry. The carpet smelled like mildew for a month after that. But yeah, I just can't keep organized or go to things anymore.
Do you have any medical conditions—like a head injury, seizures, thyroid problems, or use of alcohol or drugs—that started around the same time these suspicions began?

No, I don't have any of those things. No head injuries or seizures, nothing like that. I did bump my head once when I was working at the grocery store, though. I was stocking the top shelf with those big cans of tomatoes—the crushed ones, not the diced. Diced tomatoes are better for chili, but the crushed ones make a better pasta sauce. Anyway, the step stool slipped, and I came right down on the linoleum. Hurt like the dickens. The manager, Mr. Henderson, he made me sit in the break room with a bag of frozen peas on my head for an hour. He was a stickler for safety rules. He used to wear these thick glasses with black frames, looked like two magnifying glasses strapped to his face. Always carried a clipboard, too. But no, no medical problems or anything like that started when the notes did. And I don't drink or do drugs, never have. Just... never saw the appeal, you know?
Have you noticed any recent problems with your memory, like forgetting recent conversations or getting confused about where you are or what day it is?

No, my memory's fine. I don't forget things like that, I always know what day it is. Well, usually. I mean, I have this calendar in my kitchen, one of those big ones with the scenic pictures? My sister bought it for me for Christmas. January was this beautiful snowy mountain in Colorado, I think. Or maybe Montana. I've always wanted to go to Montana, see the wild horses. My grandpa used to have horses on his farm back when I was a kid. He had this one mare, Chestnut, she was stubborn as a mule. She'd just plant her feet and refuse to move if she didn't feel like it. He used to have to bribe her with apples just to get a halter on her. Apples are getting so expensive these days, though, have you noticed? A dollar for one piece of fruit! It's robbery. But yeah, my memory is just fine, no problems there.
Have you noticed any changes in how you think or organize your thoughts—like finding it hard to stay on topic, or doing things that others have told you seem unusual or out of place?

Well, I guess... I mean, when I try to explain things lately, it just doesn't come out right. Like, I'll start talking about the rent being due, and then I'm thinking about the marina down by the lake. My uncle used to keep a boat there, a little aluminum fishing boat with a Johnson outboard motor. It was loud, sputtered a lot, but it always got us out to the good spots where the crappie were biting. We'd use these little neon green jigs, and man, we'd pull 'em in one after another. Anyway, I'll be talking about the rent, then the marina, and then somehow I'm talking about the choir robes at church and the wires I keep finding in the walls, and people just... they look at me like I skipped half the story. Like I'm speaking Greek or something. I don't know, it makes sense in my head, but I guess it just doesn't connect for anyone else.

This combination of disorganized thought plus delusions plus functional impairment supports schizophrenia over delusional disorder, which typically lacks prominent thought disorder and marked functional decline.
